title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 1st District
area: Eastern North Carolina, including Elizabeth City, Rocky Mount and Goldsboro.

context.text: North Carolina redrew its congressional district boundaries in October 2025, and District 1 is now rated R+5 on the Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index under the new lines. Incumbent Donald Davis (D) is seeking re-election against Laurie Buckhout (R) and Tom Bailey (L).

candidates.name: Donald Davis

priorities.text: Congressman Davis' top priority in Congress is expanding access to affordable health care because he knows it is vital to keeping rural hospitals open, making health care accessible to those who need it most, and improving treatment for victims of addiction.

As the Vice Ranking Member of the House Committee on Agriculture, Congressman Davis is fighting for fair and just policies and investments that promote equity and accommodate the diversity of the district's agricultural products.

positions.summary: Cosponsor of the COVER Now Act to help states expand Medicaid, and relaunched the State Medicaid Expansion Caucus to close the Medicaid coverage gap.
Led legislation, the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, to end tax breaks that data center and Big Tech companies received under the 2025 reconciliation law.
positions.quote: Washington is giving handouts to Big Tech companies while American families are drowning

record.text: Serves as ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee's Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, and as vice ranking member of the House Armed Services Committee, also sitting on its Readiness and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.
Introduced H.R. 10448, the Reverse Big Ugly Tax Breaks for Data Centers Act, to exclude data centers from bonus depreciation and Opportunity Zone tax breaks created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately. His house.gov issues pages (health care, jobs/economy, agriculture, education, veterans) and press releases were reviewed; no statements were found directly addressing abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, climate, or Israel aid specific enough to meet the sourcing standard.

candidates.name: Laurie Buckhout

priorities.text: Lowering costs and cutting taxes for families in Eastern North Carolina.
Border security, including resourcing border patrol agents.
Cutting regulations affecting farmers and fishermen, and supporting the military and veterans.

positions.summary: Says she will stand strong against what she describes as additional red tape on law-abiding gun owners, citing her background as a combat veteran.
positions.quote: She will stand strong against the extremists who mock our hunting heritage and would punish law-abiding gun owners with additional red tape.

positions.summary: Asked about the Supreme Court ruling against the administration's tariffs, said President Trump should have the authority and that the tariffs put the U.S. on an equal footing on trade.
positions.quote: We've been taken advantage of for decades with unfair trade practices, and this is putting America back on an equal footing.

candidates.researchNotes: Buckhout has not held elected office, so there is no voting or bill-sponsorship record. Positions are from her campaign website issues page and a February 2026 interview reported by The Assembly. No statements found on rent regulation, school choice, minimum wage, or voter citizenship proof.

statements.quote: Border security is national security. Laurie will focus on ensuring our border patrol agents have the resources they need to keep dangerous drugs out of our country.

candidates.name: Tom Bailey
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

priorities.text: Restoring voting rights of citizens to put control of government back in the hands of the people.
Major federal tax reform limiting the federal government to taxing only state governments.
Restoring the Bill of Rights with an emphasis on due process.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Bailey's 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website was located and the survey lists no stance on the guide's listed issues; no news coverage quoting him on them was found.
